content.body:
Almost doomed by the bureaucracy of the RLM prior to it's maiden flight, the Messerschmitt Bf109 went on to become the most mass-produced German fighter of the war. Its design was simple; a compact slender airframe with plenty of power and a heavy gun package. The 109's combat lineage started in the Spanish Civil war in the mid thirties.
By the outbreak of WWII the E model was already a tried and true combat-tested fighter aircraft, and by the wars end just five years later the highest scoring aerial aces in the history of air combat had all exclusively flown Bf109's.
The E model is fast and has the heaviest armament of the 109's until the later G models. Possibly the best turner of the 109's this plane is as at home in a turn fight as it is in a fast diving attack. With coordinated wingman tactics the Emil can be effective against any enemy type, but alone its speed and climb rate must be relied on to survive an encounter with bad odds. Combine its overall good performance with a cool headed and confident pilot and the E can hold its own through an entire campaign. Against the RAF you must resist the temptation to turn flight exclusively as both the Spitfire and Hurricane can about turn the 109 if pressed to the point of a pure turning duel.
However climbing turns are a different story completely and can neutralize an enemys turning advantage quickly in the 109's favour.
content.brief: TYPE: Fighter Interceptor CREW: 1 WEIGHT: 2807 kg MAX SPEED: 554 km/h ARMAMENT: 2 X 20mm MGFF Cannon 2 x 7.92mm LMG
